reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent source-semantic review against the live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP view and Radare2 6.2.0 on retail igi.exe (SHA-256 dea34892...); the candidate translation unit was recompiled with the repository -O3 -DNDEBUG flags and its object symbol compared with the body recorded for the previous source digest.
source_revision: worktree HEAD 5a3b6e40521b2159f6dce7e8ecbeafb8fe3b9b91 plus the uncommitted Qvm_ReportError correction; bound by engine/src/retail/script/qvm_native_loader.cpp sha256 48ae1e2700dfc8738d9ea1a31178495ff821c3bed69ac189263a88eebac8359f
review_basis: The current engine/src/retail/script/qvm_native_loader.cpp hashes to 48ae1e2700dfc8738d9ea1a31178495ff821c3bed69ac189263a88eebac8359f. The retail entry was re-read through the live Binary Ninja view and independently recovered with Radare2 on 2026-10-23; both live graphs are identical to the bound artifacts, so the recorded CFG is current. The candidate was recompiled from that source; its object symbol body was compared with the body compiled from the previous source digest 655494c9... and is instruction-identical after relocation resolution, proving the Qvm_ReportError edit did not alter this function. This review supersedes the earlier evidence that was stale against the current source digest.

retail_function.name: String_FindExtension
retail_function.signature: char*(char* arg1, int32_t arg2, int32_t arg3)
retail_function.summary: 0x004B1E90-0x004B1ED9 (75 bytes), 6 basic blocks / 8 edges, cdecl char*(char* out,int32_t size,char* path): scans path backwards for the last 0x2E (.) at an index >= 1; when out is non-null, copies at most size-1 bytes from the dot into out via the in-binary copy helper 0x004A5500 and writes out[size-1]=0; returns the dot pointer (or path when no dot is found).

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja and Radare2 both recover 0x004B1E90-0x004B1ED9 with 6 blocks / 8 edges; the live re-read matches the bound artifacts exactly (similarity 1.000). The candidate symbol igi::retail::script::String_FindExtension(char*, int, char*) is the body implementing that entry, 208 bytes including alignment padding.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Three stack arguments in retail order: arg3 path is read at [esp+0xC] at entry, arg1 out and arg2 size are read later; the candidate declares (char* dst, std::int32_t max_len, char* path) in that order. Binary Ninja types the third argument int32_t because it never types it, but the body dereferences it as a NUL-terminated string, so char* is ABI-identical. cdecl, three stack arguments and the char* return are preserved.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The separator compare is 0x2E, the scan length starts at 0xFFFFFFFF and is converted with not/dec, and the copy/terminator index is max_len-1; all appear at the corresponding points in the candidate.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: Retail calls the in-binary copy helper 0x004A5500 (Camera_ApplyLineFilter_5) with (out, dot, size-1) and then writes out[size-1]=0; the candidate calls std::strncpy with the same arguments and writes the same terminator. The 12-case positive-length differential compared the complete destination buffer and matched. The candidate guards the call (max_len>1) and the terminator (max_len>0); for positive sizes that produces identical memory, and the max_len<=0 divergence is recorded below.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: Byte/string scanning and copying only; no floating-point data or instructions.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The scan compares path[length] first (the NUL) and walks down to path[1], never path[0]; the candidate implements exactly that loop. Destination writes stay within max_len for positive sizes. For max_len<=0 retail would pass a wrapped count to the copy helper and write out[max_len-1]; the candidate skips both, so that undefined retail domain is not reproduced (documented limitation).

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Returns path+dot when a dot is found and path when it is not, on the same branches in the candidate; the null-out path returns the dot pointer without writing. No error path exists in retail.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports char*(char*, int32_t, int32_t) and Radare2 recovers cdecl with three stack arguments; the candidate declares char* String_FindExtension(char*, std::int32_t, char*). The third argument is typed int32_t by the decompiler but dereferenced as a string; char* is ABI-identical and the char* return is preserved.

limitations: No paired retail/candidate game-process runtime capture exists for this address; runtime_tests and behavioral are intentionally absent and RUNTIME_TESTED/VERIFIED are not claimed.
The CFG agreement cited here is Binary Ninja vs Radare2 on the retail image; cfg_similarity 1.0 is not a candidate-vs-retail CFG score, and the candidate machine CFG was not compared for isomorphism.
The candidate object was rebuilt and hashed, but the image was not linked by this review; no linked-image or receipt claim is made.

For max_len <= 0 the candidate adds guards the retail body does not have: retail calls the copy helper with max_len-1 wrapped to an unsigned count and then writes out[max_len-1] (undefined behaviour), while the candidate performs neither operation. Positive lengths match; the non-positive domain is documented and not claimed equivalent.

The compiled object body is byte-for-byte identical to the 208-byte body recorded for source 655494c9... (symbol offset 0x70 in both objects), so the Qvm_ReportError edit provably did not change this function.

The binary_ninja and radare2 evidence signatures bound here were re-derived from the current artifacts (char*(char* arg1, int32_t arg2, int32_t arg3) and fcn.004b1e90 (int32_t arg_ch_2, int32_t arg_14h, int32_t arg_ch);); the manifest previously said 'not restated'.
